missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-bayesian-updating-prediction-C007 (partial): The full treatment promised by proved=annex:p15.bayes-sequential-update is incomplete. The statement (body lines 183-185) says the factors r_i are conditional predictive probabilities, and that replacing them by unconditional one-observation marginals is generally invalid. The annex (lines 165-171) argues a different substitution: that multiplying the history-free one-flag sampling probabilities under each state, in place of the copied-flag conditional factor f_2(+|theta,+)=1, changes the posterior (363/400 versus 11/122). No written step compares m_n, or any factor r_i, with the corresponding one-observation marginal predictive probability. Examples would be r_2=1 against P(Z_2=+)=1098/100000 in the copy model, or m_2 against m_1(+)^2 in the conditionally independent model. The counterexample owed for the stated claim is not supplied.

ED26-P15-CH-bayesian-updating-prediction-C011 (partial): The argument promised by proved=annex:p15.bayes-normal-calculation is not fully written. The completing-square identity (annex lines 314-319) is verified only for the theta^2 and theta coefficients. The constant terms, mu0^2/tau^2 + xbar^2/s^2 = u^2/v + (xbar-mu0)^2/(tau^2+s^2), are only asserted to agree 'after putting them over tau^2 s^2 (tau^2+s^2)' (annex lines 322-324), with no computation shown. That constant term produces the factor phi_{tau^2+s^2}(xbar-mu0) in the stated joint observation density m_n (body lines 283-288). The m_n claim therefore rests on a sketched step.

ED26-P15-CH-bayesian-updating-prediction-C018 (partial): Two parts of the success condition are unmet. (i) Definitions: the entry gives a value for the 'cumulative conditional logarithmic score' (body lines 457-459) but never defines it. Only the expected loss L_p(q) is defined (body lines 446-450); the per-prefix sum of -log r_i appears only implicitly in the annex (lines 576-578). (ii) Source variant not preserved: Kass-Raftery sec. 3.2 (p.777) defines the logarithmic scoring rule as log pr_i(y_i) and the cumulative score as LS = sum log pr_i(y_i) = log pr(D|H_k). The entry gives the same name to the opposite-signed quantity -log m_n and does not mark the sign difference as a variant.

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-bayesian-updating-prediction-C018 (partial): Definitions and source variants not plainly supplied. Definitions: the final claim (handbook/parts/p15/bayesian-updating-prediction.tex 457-459) says the cumulative conditional logarithmic score is -log m_n(x_{1:n}), but neither the entry nor the chapter defines a realized logarithmic score of a report at an outcome or the cumulative conditional score over the predictive factors r_i. Only the expected loss L_p(q) is defined (446-450), and the annex (576-578) only rewrites -log m_n as -sum_i log r_i. Source variants: the cited Kass-Raftery Sec. 3.2 (held PDF p. 6, journal p. 777) defines the logarithmic scoring rule log pr_i(y_i), LS = sum_i log pr_i(y_i) and log pr(D|H_k) = LS_k (reward orientation). The entry neither preserves that variant nor states that its score has the opposite sign, so read with the cited source's definition the displayed value carries the wrong sign.
